title: Art Tatum at the Rhythm Club
summary: Tatum's 1931 appearance stunned musicians; Adelaide Hall tour.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Right. So what was -- you said sometimes they used to jam. Do you have any particular memories, any --
Oh, yeah, yeah, the first time there I had Art Tatum.

You couldn't even move in that place. And Tatum came to New York to join ______ to go to Paris. That was in 1931. And before Art Tatum was working in the club, the word got around, half an hour later you couldn't get nobody there. All the musicians are running out to listen to the man play. And that was my first -- and after that, nobody wanted to touch the piano, that night, nobody wanted to touch it.

The only guy that played that night (unintelligible). Yeah, he used to play for Florence ______, I think, or one of those old ______, I don't know. But when this Art Tatum played, I mean, he was so far away from everybody else's, it was unbelievable.
And then he used to go and play poker.

And I used to tell the guy, (unintelligible). He says, well, he's (unintelligible) in one eye, but anyway he always had a man with him, and they can fix his car and put a ______ in the corner of one eye and he can play. So I guess at that time

he was not completely blind. That's what he told me. And then he went to Paris as a piano player for Adderly Hall. And I met Adderly Hall when she got back here to America, and she worked with us, with the (unintelligible). We went to Chicago, we went to different cities to play vaudeville with her.
